analysis.title: Too Fast, Too Furious: A Rare, and Negative NDX Signal
key_insights: NDX fell -5.61% on Friday and was up over 6% as of about 2:30pm on the Monday of the note (November 23, 2026). Since 1985 there have been 12 prior cases of a -5% or worse daily decline followed immediately by a +5% or better daily gain.
BTIG says to use strength over the next day or two to reduce, not chase, risk in the broad market and specifically in the tech/AI trade.
Of the 12 prior occurrences, 11 saw NDX negative three days later, with an average of -5.4% and a median of -5.46%.
All 12 occurrences saw a drawdown of at least -4.6% over the next 30 trading days. The -4.6% best case was May 2000, before the dot-com bubble burst further.
10 of 12 saw a drawdown of at least -9.4%, and the average and median 30-day drawdowns were both -16%.
A -16% decline in QQQ would bring it to about $550, essentially the March lows.
Upside is not excluded. Average and median 30-day draw-up was about 10%, though most of the biggest draw-ups came after T+15.
Takeaway: downside risk has generally been weaker in the next 5 to 15 days, while upside risk has been greater looking out three weeks or more.
